The wide Soviet-style boulevard with a green median, the salmon-pink building with ground-floor arcaded shops and Cyrillic signage, the traffic-light gantry design, and the Chevrolet Malibu all point to a Russian regional city. The lush deciduous trees and temperate light suggest southern/central Russia in summer, consistent with a city like Rostov-on-Don.

>>> {"country":"Russia","place":"Rostov-on-Don","lat":47.2357,"lng":39.7015}

The grand cream-and-grey sandstone tenements with bay windows, left-hand driving, double-yellow lines and a UK-style "Funeralcare" shop all point to Edinburgh, Scotland. The wide straight thoroughfare with a low rounded hill (Calton Hill) on the horizon to the left is characteristic of Leith Walk looking south. The corner block on the right and the overall street geometry match the Leith Walk / Newington corridor.

{"country":"United Kingdom","place":"Leith Walk, Edinburgh, Scotland","lat":55.9620,"lng":-3.1845}

The steep hillside blanketed in dense, unpainted red‑brick housing climbing the slope is the signature look of the La Paz–El Alto basin in Bolivia, and the high‑altitude bright blue sky with sparse, dry vegetation confirms an Andean setting. The furled flag showing red and green stripes matches the Bolivian tricolor, and the broad paved plaza with multiple flagpoles is typical of a civic square in this city. Together these clues place the photo firmly in the La Paz / El Alto area of Bolivia.

{"country":"Bolivia","place":"La Paz (El Alto), Bolivia","lat":-16.5000,"lng":-68.1500}

The mix of worn plaster buildings with terracotta tile roofs, a green striped awning, and small corrugated-roof garages points to a Central European / Balkan city, while the curved glass high-rise in the upper right strongly resembles Zagreb's Asterips Tower. The European-style (blurred) plates on the VW Golf, Mercedes, VW van and Audi Q3, plus the temperate vegetation and late-afternoon sun, fit continental Croatia. Taken together these clues narrow the location to Zagreb, Croatia.

{"country":"Croatia","place":"Zagreb","lat":45.812,"lng":15.979}

The architecture is decisively French: a 1960s–70s concrete HLM-style residential tower on the left, a white institutional block with ribbon windows and a grey plinth on the right (typical campus/housing notice board), yellow-and-black striped edge bollards, brick-paved sidewalks, and EU-format licence plates. The bare deciduous trees, ivy-covered wall and low winter sun point to a temperate oceanic climate in western France rather than the Mediterranean. The mix of social housing, a parking lot and a modern glass-crowned tower in the distance fits a mid-size western French city such as Nantes.

{"country":"France","place":"Nantes","lat":47.217,"lng":-1.553}

The dominant clue is the bilingual "China Children's Store / 中国儿童用品商店" signage, a well-known landmark on Wangfujing Street in Beijing's Dongcheng District, reinforced by the red Spring Festival couplet pillars, the "乐器城" (Musical Instrument City) basement entrance, and a 24h self-service bank sign typical of central Beijing commercial streets. The LONGINES storefront and dense pedestrian shopping-mall facade confirm a major Chinese city's flagship retail strip. This pins the location to Beijing, China.

{"country":"China","place":"Beijing, Wangfujing, Dongcheng District","lat":39.9145,"lng":116.4122}

The orange LED departure board lists "RACCONI[GI]" and "REGGIO," both Italian destinations, and the platform canopy, clocks, and green FS-style logo are characteristic of Italian Ferrovie dello Stato stations. Racconigi trains originate from the Turin hub, and the heavy concrete canopies with travertine-clad buildings match Torino Porta Nuova. The overcast, wet northern-Italian weather and brick paving support this. I therefore place it at Turin's main station.

>>> {"country":"Italy","place":"Torino (Torino Porta Nuova)","lat":45.0106,"lng":7.6735}

The red car's windshield carries a "PRODEJ" (for sale) sign, which is Czech/Slovak, narrowing this to the Czech Republic or Slovakia. The grand white neoclassical institutional building with pilasters, the dark globe lamp posts, and the temperate deciduous trees fit central Prague's museum/university quarter. The wide asphalt parking in front of a monumental facade matches the area around Prague's National Museum / Wenceslas Square.

{"country":"Czech Republic","place":"Prague","lat":50.0810,"lng":14.4350}

The blue EU licence-plate strip and the round river-cobble paving point to a Central European old town, while the reflected red-brick tenements with mansard roofs and the modernist colonnade with scalloped concrete canopy are characteristic of Prague. The heavy presence of a Volvo Cross Country and a VW/Audi SUV fits the Czech car park, and the overall streetscape matches Prague's Old/New Town centre.

{"country":"Czech Republic","place":"Prague","lat":50.0875,"lng":14.4213}

The European-style yield triangle and blue mandatory-direction sign, the black traffic-light housing, the cobblestone kerb and the cluster of modern banking towers on the horizon (the famous "Mainhattan" skyline) all point to Germany, specifically Frankfurt am Main. The red-brick parapet on the left and the wide open riverfront intersection indicate a bridge approach on the south bank of the Main, looking toward the financial district. The vegetation and overcast sky are consistent with central Germany in autumn.
{"country":"Germany","place":"Frankfurt am Main","lat":50.1050,"lng":8.6820}

The Polish word on the banner ("szkoła"), the socialist‑era curved building with arched ground floor on the right, the classical red‑roofed building and formal hedge garden with a statue on the left, and the green‑spired tower at the end of the long tiled pedestrian axis all point to Wrocław, Poland, in the historic centre near the university/cathedral promenade.

{"country":"Poland","place":"Wrocław","lat":51.1120,"lng":17.0390}

The rounded script on the shop banners and the Coca-Cola signage, combined with the narrow concrete road, corrugated-metal roadside stall, parked motorcycle, and dense tropical vegetation with coconut and banana palms, strongly indicate rural mainland Southeast Asia, most likely Thailand. The lushness of the foliage and palm species suggest a southern or central Thai province rather than the drier northeast. I'll commit to a rural location in southern Thailand.

{"country":"Thailand","place":"Rural southern Thailand","lat":8.35,"lng":99.30}

The black-and-white painted median curb, the dense overhead wiring on concrete utility poles, the tropical vegetation, and the right-hand traffic with Thai-style pickup trucks and sedans all point strongly to Thailand. The wide divided road through a low-rise suburban setting suggests a central Thai province on the edge of the Bangkok metro area. I'll place it in the Pathum Thani / Rangsit corridor.

{"country":"Thailand","place":"Pathum Thani","lat":14.0208,"lng":100.5250}

The tangled overhead wiring on concrete/wooden utility poles, the right‑hand traffic, the white Mercosur‑style plates, the painted masonry houses with red‑tile roofs, and especially the pink‑flowering ipê tree all point strongly to Brazil, most likely the São Paulo metropolitan area. The wet overcast street and low‑rise residential layout fit a typical São Paulo suburb. I'll place it in the city of São Paulo.

{"country":"Brazil","place":"São Paulo","lat":-23.5600,"lng":-46.6500}

The signage reads "KEDAI CENDERAHATI" (Malay for souvenir shop) and "I ♥ KL GIFTS MALAYSIA," with a Malaysian company registration number and Malaysian flags hanging on the right, all pointing firmly to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The dense pedestrian souvenir-shop street scene matches the tourist-heavy Chinatown/Petaling Street district. I'll place it in central Kuala Lumpur.

{"country":"Malaysia","place":"Kuala Lumpur (Chinatown/Petaling Street area)","lat":3.1422,"lng":101.6981}

The white Renault Clio with a "Conan" livery and an "02 33…" phone number points to Normandy (Manche/Calvados prefix), and the half‑timbered "colombage" house with red‑brick quoins and steep slate roof is classic Norman vernacular. Combined with the European no‑entry sign, yellow‑painted curb, wooden utility pole and overcast northern‑French light, this is a small village in Normandy, France.

{"country":"France","place":"Normandy, Manche (near Saint-Lô)","lat":49.11,"lng":-1.08}

The billboard explicitly reads "MADE IN JAMAICA," which directly identifies the country, and the left-hand traffic, black-and-yellow curb markings, tropical grassland, and Caribbean-style utility poles all corroborate this. The wide divided highway with a grassy median and a parallel service road on the right is characteristic of the major arterial routes around Kingston (e.g., Washington Boulevard / Portmore corridor). The flat, open, sun-baked landscape with scattered low trees fits the southeastern coastal plain near the capital.

>>> {"country":"Jamaica","place":"Kingston (Washington Boulevard / Portmore corridor)","lat":17.9500,"lng":-76.8000}

The red-brick circular structure in the background and the long brick facade with clock tower match the iconic Las Ventas bullring complex in Madrid. The ongoing construction and crane are consistent with the major renovation works around the Salamanca district. The warm Mediterranean light and brick architecture firmly place this in central Spain.

>>> {"country":"Spain","place":"Madrid, Las Ventas","lat":40.4321,"lng":-3.6633}

The sign "FOTOGRAFÍ" uses the Icelandic accented í and the Icelandic word for photography, and the wall mural of two sheep before a misty mountain ridge is a classic Icelandic scene. The red corrugated-metal shopfront beside grey timber buildings and the low, long twilight light fit a high-latitude Nordic setting. Together these point to a photography gallery in Reykjavík's downtown.

>>> {"country":"Iceland","place":"Reykjavík","lat":64.1470,"lng":-21.9390}

The lush hanging tropical vines, palm trees, and humid lowland vegetation rule out highland colonial towns like Ouro Preto, while the old cobblestone (pedra) street, the white balustrade wall with stone base and decorative finials, and the rough granite retaining wall are hallmarks of a Brazilian colonial historic center. The parked Mercedes Sprinter and overall streetscape fit the old town of Salvador, Bahia, whose steep, vine-draped cobblestone lanes and white-walled mansions match this scene closely.

{"country":"Brazil","place":"Salvador, Bahia","lat":-12.9714,"lng":-38.5014}

The red-and-black auto rickshaw (tuk-tuk) marked "AIR MAIL EXPRESS," left-hand traffic, and Sinhala-script banners strongly indicate Sri Lanka. The distinctive mushroom-shaped white water tower and dense urban roadside advertising match the Colombo metropolitan area.

{"country":"Sri Lanka","place":"Colombo","lat":6.9271,"lng":79.8612}

The EU-format licence plates, Renault-style SUV, red fire hydrant and Mediterranean urban mix of glass high-rises with older mid-rise blocks point to Spain. The distinctive black-and-white checkered curved façade and the pink hotel logo on the distant tower, together with a canopy-covered parking lot and modular site cabins in a dense business district, are characteristic of Barcelona's redeveloped 22@/Poblenou edge. The bare winter trees and clear light fit a northeastern Spanish city.

{"country":"Spain","place":"Barcelona","lat":41.4036,"lng":2.1899}

The red banner on the ochre building contains Hungarian text referencing "Gödöllői," and the overall architecture, blue directional road sign, bollards, and street furniture are typical of Hungary. The wide avenue with trams/buses and the building styles point to a major Hungarian city, most likely Budapest. I'll place this in Budapest.

>>> {"country":"Hungary","place":"Budapest","lat":47.4979,"lng":19.0402}

The blue square pedestrian-crossing and lane-direction signs, the yellow priority-road diamonds, right-hand traffic, the Lidl logo, and the large brick-and-white panel-block apartment estates are all hallmarks of Poland. The wide signalised intersection with a modern slatted commercial building on the left and sprawling socialist-era housing blocks points to a major Polish city's residential district, most consistent with Warsaw's outskirts.

{"country":"Poland","place":"Warsaw","lat":52.2450,"lng":21.0300}

The small orange spirit house beside the potted bamboo is a hallmark of Thailand, and the lush tropical planting plus dense low-rise commercial buildings point to a Bangkok nightlife soi. English-language "BIGGAINK TATTOO" signage and market-style stalls with hanging goods match the Patpong/Silom entertainment district, while the distinctive triangular lattice-roofed venue entrance with a disco ball is typical of these Bangkok bar complexes. I therefore place this in central Bangkok near the Patpong–Silom area.

{"country":"Thailand","place":"Bangkok, Patpong/Silom","lat":13.7275,"lng":100.5345}

The overhead catenary wires, the yellow dashed lane marking (Swiss bus/tram corridors), the abundance of parked bicycles, and the advertising panel style all point to a Swiss city with a tram network. The rust-colored corten-steel angular building on the right paired with the grand classical stone building under scaffolding on the left matches the area around Helvetiaplatz / Bundesgasse near the Federal Palace in Bern. The bright summer cumulus sky and mid-latitude vegetation are consistent with the Swiss plateau.

{"country":"Switzerland","place":"Bern","lat":46.9480,"lng":7.4420}

The presence of a classic Volvo sedan among the parked cars, the gravel parking lot, and the functionalist modernist institutional architecture (curved concrete wing plus dark-brick glass facade) all point strongly to Sweden. The temperate green grass, leafy tree, and high-latitude bright overcast sky are consistent with southern/central Sweden. I'll place this at a Swedish town setting.

{"country":"Sweden","place":"Uppsala","lat":59.8586,"lng":17.6389}

The banner text "თავისუფლების" is written in the distinctive Georgian Mkhedruli script, immediately placing this in Georgia. Combined with the unfinished cinder-block construction, the open-air car wash canopy, and a Fiat Ducato camper van, this reads as a suburban Georgian roadside business. The bright, dry climate and clear sky fit a warm-season day in the Caucasus. I'll anchor the guess to the Tbilisi area.
>>> {"country":"Georgia","place":"Tbilisi","lat":41.7151,"lng":44.8271}

The low whitewashed brick warehouses with sloped roofs, the modernist white grid-windowed building, and the ochre/yellow structure are characteristic of Helsinki's converted industrial and harbour districts, while the bright clear light and lush deciduous foliage indicate a northern temperate summer. The graffiti style, gravel yard, and bollard design all fit a Scandinavian city centre, with Finland's Helsinki being the strongest match for this particular mix of old brick and modern architecture.
{"country":"Finland","place":"Helsinki","lat":60.1699,"lng":24.9384}

The patterned brick-paver sidewalk with a curved concrete retaining wall, the mix of aging Soviet-era concrete apartment blocks (balconies, satellite dishes) on the left and a sleek curved-glass modern building on the right, the lush walnut-type trees, and the bright dry sunshine all point to a post-Soviet Caucasus city. This combination of renovated pedestrian walkways alongside old residential blocks is characteristic of Tbilisi's embankment and park-side streets. The European-style white rear plate and red-white striped bollard further support this region.

>>> {"country":"Georgia","place":"Tbilisi","lat":41.6934,"lng":44.8015}

The shop signage is in Greek script ("ΕΜΠΟΡΙΑ", "Ελάφος Ετ. Μαυρακάνης"), which immediately places this in Greece, and the bright yellow ATM box matches Eurobank's branding common in Athens. The narrow, graffiti-tagged commercial street packed with parked scooters, worn asphalt, and old multi-story buildings with balconies and AC units is characteristic of central Athens (Monastiraki/Exarchia area) rather than a quiet island town. Together these clues point firmly to the Greek capital.

>>> {"country":"Greece","place":"Athens, central (Monastiraki/Exarchia area)","lat":37.9838,"lng":23.7275}

The pink storefront sign uses Khmer script, and the phone number "010 88 63" matches Cambodian mobile prefixes, firmly placing this in Cambodia. The dense overhead wiring, sidewalk-parked motorbikes, blue-painted metal staircase, and shophouse architecture are characteristic of urban Phnom Penh, where a "SUZY! TIME CAFE" and an optics shop would sit side by side. I'll commit to a central Phnom Penh location.

{"country":"Cambodia","place":"Phnom Penh","lat":11.5564,"lng":104.9282}

The blue square "H" sign marks a German public-transport stop, and the reddish building on the right carries the inscription "Museum für Neue Kunst," which is the Freiburg museum on Marienstraße. The angled glass terminal on the left with "City Check-in / airport" signage is the Freiburg ZOB / airport city terminal at Habsburgerplatz, confirmed by the street-name plate. Right-hand traffic, the zebra crossing style, and the green pedestrian signal all fit Germany.

>>> {"country":"Germany","place":"Freiburg im Breisgau, Habsburgerplatz","lat":47.9985,"lng":7.8475}

The white Toyota Alphard/Vellfire minivan is a near-certain marker for the Japanese domestic market, and the left-hand traffic, the cylindrical-topped translucent sound barriers, the red-and-white striped monitoring pole, and the lattice transmission pylon all match Japanese expressway infrastructure. The dense urban buildings in the distance place this on a metropolitan elevated highway. I'll commit to the Tokyo area.

>>> {"country":"Japan","place":"Tokyo","lat":35.6895,"lng":139.7105}

The reddish colonnade and curved metallic structure at left match the ARoS Aarhus Kunstmuseum, while the cobblestone quay, harbor with masted sailing vessels, low sun, and pink city-share bike all point to the Aarhus waterfront in Denmark. The rusted arch sculpture sits along this harbour promenade. These clues narrow it firmly to Aarhus, Denmark.

>>> {"country":"Denmark","place":"Aarhus","lat":56.1558,"lng":10.2110}

The grey limestone neoclassical facade with a sculpted soldier in the pediment, green-framed arched and rectangular windows, and a red central door are characteristic of Old Montreal's institutional architecture, most closely matching the Bonsecours Market (Marché Bonsecours) building. The overcast northern sky and temperate planters of hostas and red flowers support a Quebec setting, while the French-language signage hints confirm Canada. This places the photo firmly in historic Montreal.

{"country":"Canada","place":"Montreal, Quebec (Old Montreal, Bonsecours Market)","lat":45.5071,"lng":-73.5534}

The billboard text "IANAO NO BOSS" and "1 TAONA" is in Malagasy, and the bank/telecom logos (BOA, Orange Money, Visa/Mastercard) plus the +261 phone format point squarely to Madagascar. The tropical vegetation (palms, red bougainvillea), right-hand traffic, wide median avenue with tall floodlight masts, and dense informal utility wiring match the capital's main boulevards. This is most consistent with Antananarivo.

>>> {"country":"Madagascar","place":"Antananarivo","lat":-18.89,"lng":47.52}

The faded pink stucco apartment blocks with external AC units, the bare deciduous trees, and especially the "no stopping" sign bearing a municipal coat of arms and green logos in Latin script with diacritics all point to a Balkan housing estate, most consistent with Serbia. The continuous raised concrete median curb dividing the road and the overall neglected post-communist residential character strongly suggest Belgrade's outer blocks. The climate and leafless trees indicate a cool-season shot in the Pannonian/Balkan interior.

>>> {"country":"Serbia","place":"Belgrade","lat":44.8176,"lng":20.4561}

The white camper van carries the distinctive blue-chevron livery of the Danish police, and the sidewalk is jammed with bicycles typical of Copenhagen. The large modernist concrete building flying a rainbow pride flag alongside a blue-and-yellow municipal flag, plus the red-brick industrial building on the right and the cobblestone gutter, all fit central Copenhagen's institutional quarter. This places the scene in Denmark's capital.

{"country":"Denmark","place":"Copenhagen","lat":55.6730,"lng":12.5840}

The play equipment and background signage carry Hebrew text (e.g., on the green tractor and orange seesaw), which decisively places this in Israel. The dense modern high-rises, the municipal shade-sail playground style, the rubberized surface, and the city bus all point to a large Mediterranean city, most consistent with Tel Aviv. The bright sun, fig-type trees, and urban park layout reinforce a central Tel Aviv location.

{"country":"Israel","place":"Tel Aviv","lat":32.0853,"lng":34.7818}

The wide asphalt path with a single yellow dashed centreline is a typical Dutch bicycle highway, and the green chain‑link fence with angled top posts plus the electrified catenary masts match ProRail railway fencing. The flat terrain, young birch trees, brick‑edged pedestrian strip and modern glass office blocks with teal horizontal banding point to a business park beside a station/rail yard in the Netherlands, most consistent with the Amsterdam Zuidas / Schiphol corridor. I therefore place this in the Netherlands near Amsterdam.

{"country":"Netherlands","place":"Amsterdam (Zuidas / Schiphol corridor)","lat":52.3320,"lng":4.8720}

The yellow Dacia-style taxi is a hallmark of Moroccan cities, and the arid, hazy sky plus light concrete paving fit North Africa. The modern glass office building and the large pile-driving/construction cranes indicate a new urban development or business district under construction. These clues point to a Moroccan metropolitan area, most likely Casablanca's developing waterfront/business zones.

{"country":"Morocco","place":"Casablanca","lat":33.5910,"lng":-7.6120}

The French-language signage ("ASSURANCES AUTO-MOTO") plus right-hand traffic and the "MEGA TERAL" billboard point to a Francophone West African country, specifically Senegal. The dusty dry-season landscape, flat modern buildings, bougainvillea bush and bare trees match the Dakar urban periphery, while the wide multi-lane avenue resembles a major arterial road like the VDN/Route de l'Aéroport.

{"country":"Senegal","place":"Dakar","lat":14.712,"lng":-17.443}

The lush green hillside town with dense red-tile roofs climbing a slope, mixed with a few socialist-era apartment blocks, is characteristic of western/central Serbia. The granite monument serving as a camper water station bears a municipal coat of arms (city towers over a mountain triangle) typical of Serbian town heraldry, and the temperate vegetation plus Balkan-style architecture narrow it to Serbia rather than Western Europe.

>>> {"country":"Serbia","place":"Užice, western Serbia","lat":43.853,"lng":19.846}

The Traditional Chinese shop signage, the "美而美" bakery chain, the green district road signs, scooters parked on the right, and the concrete mid-rise architecture all point firmly to Taiwan. The branch name "縣西店" indicates 縣西路, a main road in Miaoli City, consistent with the local phone number format. This narrows the location to downtown Miaoli in northwestern Taiwan.

{"country":"Taiwan","place":"Miaoli City","lat":24.5600,"lng":120.8200}

The blue station sign reading "SAN ANTONIO" under an elevated concrete viaduct identifies this as the San Antonio station of the Metro de Medellín, an elevated rapid-transit line. Spanish storefront text ("IMPREVENTA", "REPARACION DE CALZADO...") and the Colombian "Modella" sign confirm a Spanish-speaking Colombian city, while the distinctive blue building-graphic bollards and overcast wet pavement match Medellín's public-space furniture and climate. This places the photo in central Medellín, Colombia.

{"country":"Colombia","place":"Medellín, San Antonio metro station","lat":6.2518,"lng":-75.5686}

Left-hand traffic, the tall grey dual-head streetlights, red-and-white water-filled barriers, and the extremely dense skyline of uniform high-rise residential towers with curved teal-glass facades are characteristic of Hong Kong. The highway skirting a depot/layby with trucks and the cluster of public-housing-style towers matches the Tsing Yi / Kwai Tsing corridor. This places the photo on a Hong Kong expressway on New Territories' Tsing Yi island.

{"country":"Hong Kong","place":"Tsing Yi, New Territories","lat":22.3545,"lng":114.1065}

The scene shows a tropical park or palm-lined avenue with a mix of royal palms, coconut palms, and fan palms set in manicured grass beside a weathered concrete curb and asphalt road. This combination of palm species, the simple concrete curb style, and the bright Caribbean sunlight strongly points to a Caribbean island nation, with Cuba being the most likely given the landscaping aesthetic. The lack of signage and the resort/park-like planting of young palms in rows fits a Havana-area green space.

{"country":"Cuba","place":"Havana","lat":23.1136,"lng":-82.3666}

The white-capped rafters, red-painted eaves, dark curved roof tiles, and grey brick corner turret with a tiled cap are hallmarks of Korean traditional palace/fortress architecture, and the green plaque with hanja characters confirms a Korean heritage site. The lush temperate foliage and overcast sky fit a summer day in the Seoul region. This combination of brick turret and palace-style eaves points to a historic palace complex in Seoul.

{"country":"South Korea","place":"Seoul, Gyeongbokgung Palace area","lat":37.5762,"lng":126.9768}

The overhead green sign references "La Campina" and "Calle Bolivar," both well-known streets/zones in Cochabamba, Bolivia, and the Spanish "Muebles" shop sign plus the high-altitude clear sky and cool 9°C reading reinforce an Andean Bolivian city. The exposed-brick mid-rises, tangled utility wires, red sidewalk food kiosks, and right-hand traffic all match Cochabamba's urban character. This narrows the location to the La Campina / Bolívar corridor in Cochabamba.

{"country":"Bolivia","place":"Cochabamba","lat":-17.4012,"lng":-66.1595}

Yellow rear licence plates, brick (klinker) paving, the Dutch-style "30" zone-end sign above a yield triangle, a cyclist, and traditional brick/thatched houses all point firmly to the Netherlands. The mix of bare deciduous and pine trees with sandy soil suggests the central/eastern part of the country, likely the Utrechtse Heuvelrug / Gooi area rather than a big city. The open brick-paved village square with a historic thatched building fits a small town on the heath-woodland fringe.

>>> {"country":"Netherlands","place":"Zeist, Utrechtse Heuvelrug","lat":52.0866,"lng":5.2383}

The red articulated bus is a TransMilenio unit and the license plates and yellow curbs are Colombian, while the overcast high‑altitude light and the bicycle‑symbol traffic signal fit Bogotá's climate and Ciclovía culture. The yellow‑and‑white colonial church with arched windows matches the Iglesia de San Victorino, placing this on the central avenues (Avenida Jiménez / Calle 13 near Carrera 7). Together these pin the scene to downtown Bogotá, Colombia.

{"country":"Colombia","place":"Bogotá, D.C. (Centro, near San Victorino / Avenida Jiménez)","lat":4.5980,"lng":-74.0800}

The flat, hazy desert landscape lined with dense date-palm groves stretching to the horizon points to an irrigated oasis region in the Arabian Peninsula. The yellow-and-black striped curbs, the European-style blue "keep right" arrow and red no-entry signs, the curved double-arm street lights, and the louvered cream electrical kiosk are all hallmarks of Gulf road infrastructure, most consistent with Saudi Arabia. The combination of vast palm plantations and a wide, pristine planned interchange strongly suggests the Eastern Province / Al-Ahsa oasis area.

{"country":"Saudi Arabia","place":"Al-Ahsa, Eastern Province","lat":25.42,"lng":49.59}

The lush tropical vegetation, the distinctive scalloped white boundary wall on the left, the concrete Jersey barriers lining a divided motorway, and the green highway sign board on the right are all characteristic of West African expressways, particularly Ghana's Tema–Accra motorway corridor. The style of street lighting, the red-and-yellow chevron rear markings on the box truck, and the roadside car park with a red pickup reinforce a Ghanaian highway setting near the capital. I'll place this on the Accra–Tema motorway just outside central Accra.

{"country":"Ghana","place":"Accra (Tema Motorway)","lat":5.6650,"lng":-0.1780}

The black-and-white patterned calçada portuguesa pavement, Pombaline-era buildings with wrought-iron balconies, and the visible triumphal arch in the distance (Rua Augusta Arch) all point unmistakably to Lisbon's downtown pedestrian street, Rua Augusta. The Portuguese shop signage and tiled facades confirm Portugal. This is the classic view looking north toward the arch.

>>> {"country":"Portugal","place":"Rua Augusta, Lisbon","lat":38.7107,"lng":-9.1391}

The ochre-and-white banded mid-century institutional building, the manicured civic lawn with conical topiary, the tall fan palms alongside temperate trees, and the large abstract public sculpture all point to a South African city centre civic precinct. The skyline with a communications-style tower and curved-roof government buildings in the background matches central Johannesburg's parkland around the Art Gallery / Civic area. The overall vegetation and architecture rule out Europe or North America and confirm a Highveld South African city.

{"country":"South Africa","place":"Johannesburg","lat":-26.195,"lng":28.035}

The parking sign reads "8 tímar" (8 hours), which is Faroese, and the treeless, moss-covered hills under a heavy overcast sky are classic Faroe Islands terrain. A Scania truck dealership sits on the right, consistent with the commercial/industrial fringe of Tórshavn. These clues together place the scene in the Faroese capital region.

{"country":"Faroe Islands","place":"Tórshavn","lat":62.016,"lng":-6.795}

The bare linden-tree avenue, zebra crossing, blue-and-red no-stopping sign, EU-style plates and the "ANCHOR" shopfront point to a temperate Western European city, most consistent with Belgium. The mix of 1960s office blocks and a glass-fronted building beside a park-like tree-lined boulevard matches the Brussels region. Overcast sky and leafless trees indicate a late-autumn/winter day in a lowland temperate climate.
